rv.q: It's a rare actor who can make two hours of theological introspection entertaining, but Suchet is that actor.
I can pretty much guarantee that you won't see anything as strange, challenging and fascinating on a London stage this year.

Robert Jones’s design creates a catwalk along the central aisle that provides a focus for the confrontations between spiritual and worldly forces. The composer Orlando Gough arranges the voices of the begrimed, all-female community chorus in lines that strike a clever balance between the 12th century and the modern.
Eliot was not much of a playwright and this is more arcane, tortured hagiography than it is tragedy.
But this performance, directed by the Orange Tree Theatre's Tom Littler with associate director Francesca Ellis, and starring David Suchet is an absolute triumph.
Littler's Murder in the Cathedral takes an already beautiful text and then knocks it out of the park in all aspects of the production.

cn.t: Critics praise this audacious staging of T.S. Eliot's verse drama, with David Suchet's gravitas anchoring an excellent production that does justice to the beautiful poetry in the inspired setting of St John the Divine Church.
